chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah Nushayb al-Lafa'ifi, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [traits] are from the nobilities of the world and the Hereafter: pardoning the one who oppresses you, maintaining relations with the one who cuts you off, and forbearance when foolishness is shown to you.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three traits of nobility in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines 'makarim al-akhlaq' (nobility of character) through three active virtues: pardoning the oppressor, reconnecting with the estranged, and exercising forbearance against ignorance. These traits are highlighted in Shia scholarship as transformative forces that not only secure spiritual reward but also foster social harmony and personal dignity in this world. The emphasis on 'tahallum' (forbearance) specifically addresses the response to *jahil* (ignorant) behavior, reflecting the Imam's focus on emotional intelligence in ethical conduct.
